statement: You are given an infix expression, expression, in which each operator sits between its two operands and parentheses may group sub-expressions. Operands are single uppercase letters A to Z. The operators are +, −, *, / and ^, all binary.

Convert it to prefix notation, where each operator comes before its two operands and no parentheses are needed. Use the usual precedence: ^ binds tightest, then * and /, then + and −. Operators of equal precedence group left to right, except ^, which groups right to left.
Return the prefix expression as a string with no spaces.

examples.explanation: B*C binds first and becomes *BC; adding A in front of it gives +A*BC.
Each parenthesised group becomes its own prefix term, −AB and +CD, and the multiplication applies to both.
Subtraction groups left to right, so this is (A−B)−C, whose prefix form puts the outer − first: − (−AB) C.
